'''Nizuc Bek''' was a [[Gender|male]]<ref name="SWFC" /> [[human]] who was in the [[Boba Fett's Palace|palace]] of the [[crime lord]] [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure|Jabba]] the [[Hutt]] prior to the [[Battle of Endor]]. Bek was hired by Jabba the Hutt to guard celebrities visiting Jabba's palace. He was assigned to protect [[Sy Snootles]], the [[Max Rebo Band]]'s lead vocalist. When [[Luke Skywalker]] arrived and failed to persuade Jabba to release [[Han Solo]] and [[Chewbacca]], he used [[the Force]] to telekinetically seize Bek's [[DL-18 blaster pistol]] in an attempt to kill the Hutt.<ref name="ROTJ" />

==Biography==
===Celebrity bodyguard===
Nizuc Bek was a [[human]]<ref name="ROTJ" /> [[Gender|male]] who was [[Jabba's criminal empire|hired]] by [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure]],<ref name="SWFC" /> a Hutt [[crime lord]],<ref name="ROTJ" /> to [[Security guard|guard]] celebrities visiting the Hutt's [[Boba Fett's Palace|palace]]<ref name="SWFC" /> on the [[desert]] [[planet]] [[Tatooine]].<ref name="CL">[[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2016)|''Star Wars: Complete Locations'']]</ref> During the [[Max Rebo Band]]'s tenure as Jabba's house band, Bek was assigned to protect its lead [[Musician|vocalist]], the [[Pa'lowick]] [[Sy Snootles]].<ref name="SWFC" /> In [[4 ABY]],<ref name="Date">''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the events of {{Film|VI}} to [[4 ABY]].</ref> Bek was stood behind Jabba's [[throne]] at the palace talking to another human when the [[droid]]s [[R2-D2]] and [[C-3PO]] were brought before Jabba by his [[majordomo]], [[Bib Fortuna]], and two [[Gamorrean]] guards.<ref name="ROTJ" />
[[File:LaughingHermi-ROTJ.png|thumb|right|300px|Nizuc Bek stares at Han Solo's frozen form]]
Bek continued his conversation while R2-D2 played a message from the droids' master, [[Jedi Knight]] [[Luke Skywalker]], in which the [[Jedi]] asked to bargain with Jabba for the freedom of the [[smuggler]] [[Han Solo]] and gifted the Hutt the two droids as a sign of good faith. As the message ended and Jabba declared he would not give up Solo, Bek and the other human moved across the court room to look at Solo, who was frozen in [[carbonite]] and displayed on Jabba's wall.<ref name="ROTJ" />

===Attack of a Force-wielding blaster thief===
[[File:Nizuc_bekd.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Nizuc Bek worked as a bodyguard.]]
The next [[Standard day|day]],<ref name="Darkside">''[[Return of the Jedi: Beware the Power of the Dark Side!]]''</ref> Bek was stood beside Jabba's throne when Skywalker confronted Jabba in the throne room and demanded that Solo and the [[Wookiee]] [[Chewbacca]] be released. When Jabba refused, the Jedi used [[the Force]] to [[Telekinesis|pull]] Bek's [[DL-18 blaster pistol]] from his [[belt]] and across the room into Skywalker's hand. Before he could fire the weapon, the [[Gamorrean]] guard [[Jubnuk]] grappled with the Jedi and both were sent tumbling down through a trap door by Jabba, ending up in the pit beneath the throne room.<ref name="ROTJ" />

Bek and the rest of the court quickly moved to a grating that looked down into the pit, and watched as Jabba's pet [[rancor]], [[Pateesa]], emerged and [[Death|devoured]] Jubnuk. Their cheers were quickly silenced though, when Skywalker managed to kill Pateesa using the large door to the pit. An angry Jabba demanded that Skywalker, Solo, and Chewbacca be brought before him, and as Bek watched, the Hutt sentenced the trio to be executed at the [[Great Pit of Carkoon]]. Bek then joined a crowd of courtiers that followed the three [[prisoner]]s as they were marched from the throne room.<ref name="ROTJ" />

===Desert voyage===
[[File:SySnootlesNizucBek-BaseSeries4.png|thumb|right|220px|Bek accepts a kiss from Sy Snootles]]
In order to view the executions, Bek traveled with Jabba on board the Hutt's [[sail barge]], the ''[[Khetanna]]''. Along the way, he socialized with and accepted a kiss from Sy Snootles.<ref name="Base Series 4">{{SWCT|set=Base Series 4|cardname=Sy Snootles & Nizuc Bek}}</ref> Upon reaching the Great Pit, Bek stood with other court members and Jabba in the barge's hold and watched the [[Bantha-II cargo skiff]] carrying the prisoners as it hovered above the [[Mouth|maw]] of the [[sarlacc]] that dwelt in the pit. Jabba offered the prisoners a chance to beg for mercy, but Skywalker simply gave the Hutt one last chance to spare them, earning a laugh from the crowd. The Jedi was then pushed over the edge of the [[skiff]], but leapt back up, now armed by R2-D2 with his [[Luke Skywalker's green lightsaber|lightsaber]].<ref name="ROTJ" />

As Skywalker began cutting down the skiff guards, confusion broke out among those on the barge and the Jedi's [[Slavery|enslaved]] ally, [[Princess]] [[Leia Skywalker Organa Solo|Leia Organa]] took the opportunity to smash the controls operating the vehicle's shutters and plunge those in the hold into darkness. As the crowd rushed around in blind panic, Organa then killed Jabba by strangling him with a chain and then made her way to the top deck, where she used a [[Me/7 double laser cannon|deck cannon]] to destroy the barge before escaping with Skywalker and their other allies.<ref name="ROTJ" />

==Personality and traits==
Nizuc Bek had light skin and [[Color|brown]] [[hair]].<ref name="ROTJ" />

==Equipment==
Bek wore a yellow [[Clothing|tabard]] with a black [[belt]] and holster and matching [[gauntlet]]s and [[goggles]]. He had brown pants and [[boot]]s and also wore a gray headpiece with a brown fabric neckguard that hung from the back. As well as his DL-18 [[blaster pistol]], Bek also carried a [[blaster rifle]].<ref name="ROTJ" />

==Behind the scenes==
Nizuc Bek appeared in the [[1983]] [[original trilogy]] film, [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars:'' Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']]. In the current ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]], Bek was first identified in the [[Star Wars video games|mobile card game]] ''[[Star Wars: Force Collection]]'',<ref name="SWFC" /> which initially launched in [[2013]]. Although the launch of ''Force Collection'' predates<ref name="Force Collection release">{{SW|url=news/announcing-star-wars-force-collection|text=Announcing Star Wars: Force Collection|nolive=1}}</ref> the ''Star Wars'' canon reset of [[2014]],<ref name="Legends">{{SW|url=news/the-legendary-star-wars-expanded-universe-turns-a-new-page|text=The Legendary Star Wars Expanded Universe Turns a New Page}}</ref> [[Lucasfilm Story Group]] member [[Leland Chee]] confirmed that the game was kept updated to fit with canon.<ref name="Twitter">{{Twitter|holocronkeeper|status/846807700482666496|[[Leland Chee]]|quote=I'm not gonna go through the trouble of changing them and I don't have any reason to believe currently that anyone would. […] On the off-chance that we DID have a current need to change any of these, we would have for Force Collection.|archivedate=20210505080831}} — [[Leland Chee]] of the [[Lucasfilm Story Group]] has confirmed that [[in-universe]] information from ''[[Star Wars: Force Collection]]'' conforms with ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]].</ref> The [[2016]] reference book [[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2016)|''Star Wars: Complete Locations'']] misspelt the name as "Nizuc Beck."<ref name="CL" /> The name originated in the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity, where it was first used on a card in the [[1998]] "[[Jabba's Palace Limited]]" set of the ''[[Star Wars Customizable Card Game]]'' produced by [[Decipher]]<ref name="CCG">{{CCG|set=Jabba's Palace Limited|cardname=Nizuc Bek}}</ref>
